Prompts: REA_17 §3.4. · edge (catalyst pole only; owner 2026-10-16, THE EDGE v9: two sentences, the energy and its three ruling domains from the GOD table, then a clause per domain in The Pattern's voice; the metric; the head derived in the app)

candidates.structural_interaction: Water directing Fire cross-polarity — depth shaping illumination into structured purpose
candidates.k2_overview: Your Fire moves as the Steward: a hearth, not a bonfire. You keep warmth the way households keep flame, fed regularly, banked at night, never wasted on show. Your providing glows: steady income, warm table, festivals on schedule. It is the rarest fire, the kind that lasts.
candidates.k2_functional: You work in sustainable heat: consistent output that never needs rescue.

k2_domain_readings.Wealth: Your wealth is hearth-warm: earned brightly, spent on the household’s glow, kept steady over spectacular. Fund the gatherings and the securities both. A warm home is your portfolio’s purpose.
k2_domain_readings.Savings: You save for warmth: reserves that keep winters kind. Automate them so celebration cannot raid the woodpile. A banked fire relights fast. An empty grate does not.
k2_domain_readings.Steady love: You love like kept flame: daily warmth, faithful attention, romance on the calendar and off it. Your constancy is the gift. Add sparks deliberately so the hearth never assumes.

catalyst.define: As a catalyst, what little warmth there is gets guarded close. It reaches a few people and stays with them.

angles.drive: Keeping a thing going is the warmest part of you. You would rather keep one thing warm for years than start many, since what lasts feels real to you. Your friendships are decades old, and they still hold.
angles.cost_self: Keeping something going also keeps you in it past its time. You would rather stay than leave, so you keep putting money into what no longer gives back. Your savings are tied up in things you stopped loving long ago.
angles.cost_others: You keep love going on time and without fail. Reliable feels more like love to you than exciting does, so you give your partner steady warmth over surprise. Home life with you has everything except the unexpected.

angles.drive: Saving comes before spending for you, every time. Something put by is what lets you sleep, so you keep a little back rather than enjoy all of it now. The lean months find your household ready.
angles.cost_self: Saving first means the fun always comes second. You choose covered rather than comfortable, and the treat you could afford never gets bought. What you want is proof that you are safe enough to enjoy something.
angles.cost_others: You save first and ask the people at home to wait with you. You put being covered ahead of treating them, since you do the counting. Your family's treats come after the budget.

angles.drive: Showing up every day is how you love. Being there outranks being exciting for you, and you give the daily thing over the grand one. Those who count on you have never once been left waiting.
angles.cost_self: The daily showing up costs you the rest you needed. You put reliable ahead of rested, so you show up on days you have nothing left to bring. Your health quietly pays for that perfect attendance.
angles.cost_others: You show up daily whether your partner needs it that day or not. Being there makes you feel useful, so you offer presence where a question would serve better. They get your company without fail and seldom the thing they wanted.

friction.define: As a friction, each bright chance lands like a threat. Your need to feel secure keeps you braced against the heat until it wears you out.

angles.drive: You count everything, the money and the favours and the hours. Counting is your way of feeling safe, so knowing the total comes before enjoying the thing. Underneath the counting, you want to enjoy what you have.
angles.cost_self: Counting keeps the fear quiet and the pleasure quieter. You want to know what you have more than to use it, so the money sits counted and unspent. Busy adding up your savings, you give up the use of them.
angles.cost_others: Your count covers the household's spending as much as your own. Knowing where every bit went keeps you calm, and you ask about the receipt before the day itself. You charge your family a question for every small purchase.

angles.drive: Playing it safe is your first answer. You would rather keep a small sure thing than try for a big maybe, because being safe is what lets you rest. Every time you play it safe, you are also picking which chance to miss.
angles.cost_self: What you already have feels too precious to risk. Reaching for more feels like gambling, and you take the sure thing instead of the bigger one. Over the years, you give up more in missed chances than playing it safe ever saves you.
angles.cost_others: You make the safe call for both of you whenever money is shared. You would rather play it safe than try something new together, so your partner's bigger ideas wait. You give up your partner's chances with your own each time you say no.

angles.drive: Without deciding to, you hold back warmth and money. Giving the whole of yourself feels like spending the last of something, and you give a careful portion rather than the full amount. You hold back more than you need to feel safe.
angles.cost_self: Keeping yourself back spares you hurt and costs you being known. You would rather hold back part of yourself than give the whole, so you stay half known. You lose the closeness itself, since nobody can hold what you keep back.
angles.cost_others: You hold back hardest where you love most. You keep a reserve rather than give it all, and your partner gets the careful share only. You feel more warmth than your partner ever gets to see.

edge.lead: Fire runs through your wealth, your family and your career. It is the bill you pay the day it comes in, the home that runs on small habits kept every week, and the quiet daily hour of work that slowly becomes a career.
